subject: general
question: India has moved up to 9th position globally in total forest area as per the Global Forest Resources Assessment (GFRA) 2025. What is the country's ranking in terms of annual forest area gain, as reported in the same assessment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India has moved up to the 9th position globally in total forest area, as per the Global Forest Resources Assessment (GFRA) 2025, and continues to hold the 3rd position in annual forest area gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **India’s total forest area rank has improved from 10th to 9th, reflecting significant progress in forest expansion and ecological restoration.**
 
• **India maintains its 3rd position globally in annual forest area gain, indicating sustained growth in green cover through government and community initiatives.**
 
• **Key initiatives like the Green India Mission, compensatory afforestation, and the “Ek Ped Ma Ke Naam” campaign have contributed to this achievement.**
 
• **The success highlights India’s leadership in global forest conservation, climate action, and biodiversity preservation efforts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Forest Resources Assessment (GFRA)**__

 __
 
• Issued by the FAO every five years, it provides global data on forest trends, including forest area, deforestation, and forest-related resources.
 
• GFRA serves as a key tool in tracking progress toward sustainable forest management and global environmental goals.
 
 
 
• **India’s Forest Strategies**__
 __
 
• The Green India Mission and compensatory afforestation programs have been instrumental in India’s progress in forest conservation.
 
• Community-led initiatives, including tribal participation and Panchayat-level forestry models, have also contributed to India’s success.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Climate and Biodiversity**__
 
 
• Forests play a critical role in carbon sequestration, essential for India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement.
 
• Expanding forest cover enhances biodiversity conservation, especially in India’s unique ecosystems such as the Western Ghats, Northeast, and Sundarbans.
